items.addition: This is a walkthrough of how we built the shell of this home addition, step by step. Day one, we come out and mark the exact footprint, so the new room sits inside your property lines and the city's setbacks. Next, the footings. That's the foundation of the addition. It shows you the real size of the new space, and it's what holds up the whole structure. Before the slab, make sure your contractor treats the soil for termites, so they can't nest under your house, and lays down the plastic vapor barrier that keeps moisture out of your slab and out of your home. Then the concrete block goes up. Steel dowel rods tie the walls to the foundation. Those rods run up through the block, and the cells get filled with concrete. On top, we form and pour the tie beam. It locks the walls together and connects the structure to your roof trusses. Its height is very important. It usually has to match the existing house, and it has to work with your truss design. Then the trusses go up, and each one gets metal connectors, so the wind can't lift your roof off. Block, steel, tie beam and connectors, all working together as one solid structure, built to stand up to hurricane winds. This addition isn't finished yet. Follow along to see what comes next. Planning an addition in South Florida? Let's build it right.
